prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B003 is the only candidate all six of us placed first, and the case rests on more than agreement: it is a continuous arc from gut-hormone physiology (Holst on GLP-1 secretion and action, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the therapeutic concept, Mojsov on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) to drugs with large, independently replicated outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in question and the clinical impact is of the scale the prize is meant to recognise. The discovery-stage names fit the three-person limit without splitting a coherent achievement. As a neurologist I also note the central appetite-regulating actions of these peptides, which make this general physiology and not only a drug-development story.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness. The three-person limit excludes Knudsen, whose medicinal chemistry made liraglutide and semaglutide possible, and my opening ballot preferred her to Mojsov. Mojsov's priority for identifying the active peptide is contested and I cannot resolve it from the supplied names. Any trio is defensible but not uncontroversial, and a prize that rewards discovery over development could be read as overlooking the people who made the drugs usable.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked B003 first but treated Knudsen as a development rather than a discovery contributor, and ranked optogenetics (B036) second with a Deisseroth, Nagel, Bamberg trio.
responses.response: I have moved toward his reading on Knudsen. In my opening I weighted her medicinal chemistry heavily, but the prize rewards discovery, and Holst, Drucker and Mojsov together cover the physiology and the active peptide. I do not agree with ranking B036 so high: with six credited names and Hegemann and Miesenbock outside his trio, any three-person selection would be hard to defend, and a method without a settled disease-level achievement is weaker for me than B015 or B043.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked the unfolded protein response (B043) second and described Walter and Mori as a clean, complementary two-person credit with decades of confirmation.
responses.response: I agree that B043 is the cleanest attribution on the list and that the mechanism is textbook. My reservation is that its link to human disease and therapy is still developing, which is why I keep it as an alternative rather than ranking it above CAR-T. If the committee wanted a basic-science prize rather than a clinical one, I would take his argument seriously, but I do not think it should displace B003. I disclose my co-authorship with him below.

responses.point: Sandberg argued for B003 with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and ranked cGAS-STING (B052) third on a clean molecular pathway with Chen and Barber.
responses.response: I agree on the trio for B003, and I now prefer it to my opening choice. On B052 I am more cautious: the mechanism is well confirmed, but clinical translation of STING agonists and antagonists is unproven, and the credit is contested among Ishikawa, Sun, Wu and others, so I would not put it ahead of B015 or B043 at this stage.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius placed imatinib and CML (B010) third as fully mature and arguably overdue, with Lydon, Druker and Sawyers as a coherent trio.
responses.response: I ranked B010 fourth and agree about its clinical impact and maturity. I qualify it in two ways. The trio's roles are clear, but the upstream BCR-ABL work of Rowley, Baltimore and others sits outside the names, and targeted therapy in CML has partly been addressed by earlier major prizes. For those reasons I keep it behind B015, where a newer modality is at stake and the credit, although also imperfect because of Eshhar, is at least more open.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranked antisense splicing correction for spinal muscular atrophy (B040) third as a fatal childhood disease made treatable, with Krainer and Bennett a matched pair.
responses.response: I find B040 attractive scientifically, with a clean pair and a general principle for RNA drugs. I did not rank it in my top five mainly because follow-up is shorter than for GLP-1 or CAR-T, and because I would first want to settle how far the prize should reward a therapy rather than an upstream discovery. I do not see a reason to put it ahead of B015.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third GLP-1 place, given contested priority for the active peptide and the discovery versus development distinction.
Whether other early GLP-1 contributors outside the supplied names have a claim that the committee cannot assess from this material.
If CAR-T were preferred, how to credit Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept, and whether June and Sadelain without Rosenberg is the fairest pair.
statement.conflict_note: Per my profile I have about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and worked with Paul Greengard as a postdoctoral fellow. None of the credited candidates on the shortlist is linked to me through those connections, so no recusal issue is apparent for B003, B015 or B043. I disclose the Perlmann collaboration because he argues for B043.
